Gibson coined the term \"cyberspace\" for \"widespread, interconnected digital technology\" in his short story \"Burning Chrome\" (1982), and later popularized the concept, along with his usage of the \"matrix\", in his acclaimed debut novel Neuromancer (1984). These early works of Gibson's have been credited with \"renovating\" science fiction literature in the 1980s.\nAfter expanding on the story in Neuromancer with two more novels (Count Zero in 1986 and
